papers.title: Complex-valued physics-informed machine learning for efficient solving of quintic nonlinear Schrödinger equations
papers.access_level: Full 18-page paper: methods, baseline design, experimental tables and conclusion inspected; public repository listing inspected.
papers.evidence: Complex-valued layers and predictive dynamic monitoring sampling evaluated on 16 one-dimensional GPE cases. Real baseline approximately matched parameter counts; three repetitions. PDM comparison contains a slightly worse case. Typical training approximately two hours for 50000 epochs on an Nvidia 3090. Spectral solutions supply references.
papers.limitations: Demonstrates improvement over selected PINN baselines, not superiority to spectral solvers. One-dimensional GPE tests are not water-wave Dysthe validation. Repository was not executed and its linked data were not tested.
papers.explicit_future_work: Section VI, PDF page 17: extend to two/three dimensions and other PDEs; explore real-valued problems; improve sampling by jointly monitoring equation residuals and solution gradients and adaptively choosing resampling nodes.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for nonlinear Schrödinger localized wave problems with gradient-residual adaptive collocation sampling
papers.access_level: Publisher abstract, metadata, references and availability statement; subscription full text inaccessible.
papers.evidence: GRAVIS combines residual magnitude with output-layer parameter-gradient norm, tempered Gaussian mixture sampling, exploration and importance correction. Seven localized-wave benchmarks under matched architectures/training budgets; authors report 1.56-2.37 times lower relative L2 error than RAD and up to 36.4 times lower than uniform sampling.
papers.limitations: Full cost and statistical accounting not audited. No measured ocean-wave validation established. No public implementation verified. Data availability statement says no datasets generated or analysed.

papers.title: Noether-constrained physics-informed neural networks for the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
papers.access_level: Publisher abstract, issue metadata and authorship contribution statement only.
papers.evidence: Dynamically weighted Noether-inspired penalties plus residual-adaptive sampling. Abstract reports soliton amplitude errors below 0.8%, mass/momentum/energy fluctuations of order 1e-3, and extrapolation beyond the training domain.
papers.limitations: Numerical horizons, comparison fairness, phase diagnostics and repetitions could not be audited. Penalty-based small fluctuations are not exact conservation. Code not verified. Date is the issue date; online-first date not established.

papers.title: Structure-preserving conservative phase-amplitude PINNs for semiclassical Schrödinger-type equations
papers.venue: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics 485, 117607 (issue date)
papers.access_level: Publisher abstract, extensive introduction and section previews. Authors corroborated on the IIT BHU author publication page https://iitbhu.ac.in/dept/mat/people/rajeevapm .
papers.evidence: Real phase/complex amplitude representation with soft local continuity and global mass/energy penalties. Two-dimensional linear plane wave, moving oblique defocusing dark soliton, and inverse semiclassical/nonlinearity parameters; artificial noise at 5% and 10%.
papers.limitations: Full numerical tables and final future-work discussion inaccessible; code unverified. Conservation is approximate. Defocusing semiclassical tests do not establish focusing water-wave modulational-instability performance. Date is the issue date.

papers.title: Nonlinear interaction multi-domain physics-informed neural networks for the hybrid rogue wave and breather solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation
papers.venue: Communications in Nonlinear Science and Numerical Simulation 151, 109049
papers.access_level: Publisher abstract and introduction; author metadata checked against bibliographic indexing.
papers.evidence: NI-MPINNs combines nonlinear interaction features, residual connections and domain decomposition. Hybrid rogue-wave/breather reconstructions and noisy/noiseless inverse coefficients. Authors report accuracy improvements up to three orders of magnitude relative to classical PINNs.
papers.limitations: Full training-budget accounting, ablations and spectral cost comparison not accessible. Code not verified. Month is issue metadata, not independently verified online-first date.

papers.title: Data-driven SFB solutions and parameters discovery for nonlinear Schrödinger equation via time domain decomposition physics-informed neural networks
papers.access_level: Publisher abstract, introduction and methodology preview; author metadata corroborated with indexing.
papers.evidence: Time-domain decomposition with interface training points. Akhmediev and Kuznetsov-Ma breathers, Peregrine waves, higher-order rogue waves, and noisy/noiseless inverse coefficients. Authors report one-two orders of magnitude improvement and reduced training time against classical PINNs.
papers.limitations: Full cost audit and implementation not verified. Translation to spatial water-wave evolution requires explicit formulation handling. Date is issue metadata.

papers.title: Enhancing accuracy of physically informed neural networks for nonlinear Schrödinger equations through multi-view transfer learning
papers.access_level: Publisher abstract, introduction and partial conclusion.
papers.evidence: Pretrained NLS models transfer across initial/boundary-condition views. Compares losses and reports improved results with Huber loss relative to conventional MSE PINNs.
papers.limitations: Amortized total cost, random-spectrum generalization and code not verified. Transfer learning does not alone establish a neural operator. Exact online date not established.

papers.title: Predicting positon solutions of a family of nonlinear Schrödinger equations through deep learning algorithm
papers.venue: Physics Letters A 511, 129551 (issue date); arXiv:2405.04968 submitted 2024-05-08
papers.access_level: Full preprint method, experiments and conclusion.
papers.evidence: Analytic positon reconstructions in higher-order and coupled NLS equations; substitutes x=0 observations for boundary data. Tables show no improvement for basic NLS and improvements in several higher-order cases.
papers.limitations: Observation geometry changes the learning task, so improvements are not architecture-only evidence. Analytic reconstructions do not demonstrate unfamiliar-packet forecasting. Integrable hierarchy equations are not the approved Dysthe baseline. Code unverified.

papers.title: Enhanced PINNs for data-driven solitons and parameter discovery for (2+1)-dimensional coupled nonlinear Schrödinger systems
papers.venue: Results in Applied Mathematics 27, 100635; arXiv:2501.05011 submitted 2025-01-09 with a longer title
papers.access_level: Full preprint methods, examples and conclusions; publisher metadata for final title.
papers.evidence: Locally adaptive activations, region-weighted residual loss and residual refinement; a second network estimates variable coefficients. Analytic dark/anti-dark structures and artificial noise tests.
papers.limitations: Does not establish identifiability from sparse physical measurements or realistic mismatch. Optical coupled system supplies method background only. Code unverified. Date is issue month.

papers.title: PINNs Study for the Bekki-Nozaki Chaos in the Non-linear Schrödinger equation
papers.access_level: Full preprint including sequential forward/inverse experiments.
papers.evidence: Sequential two-second blocks approximate a thirty-second forced/dissipative trajectory. Coefficient recovery depends on observation-window length. Forward PINN outputs provide inverse training data.
papers.limitations: Mesh-free agreement does not prove intrinsic chaos or eliminate collocation/optimization errors. Inverse study is not independent measured-data validation. Journal publication and public code not established.
